title: Longest Subsequence With Decreasing Adjacent Difference
summary: Given an array of integers nums, find the length of the longest subsequence seq such that the absolute differences between consecutive elements in seq form a non-increasing sequence.
statement: Given an array of integers nums, find the length of the longest subsequence seq such that the absolute differences between consecutive elements in seq form a non-increasing sequence. Specifically, for a subsequence seq0, seq1, seq2, ..., seqm of nums, the condition |seq1 - seq0| >= |seq2 - seq1| >= ... >= |seqm - seqm - 1| must hold. Return the length of such a subsequence.
constraints: Choose a subsequence whose absolute adjacent differences are non-increasing.
hints: A state needs the ending value and its most recent difference.
Because values are bounded by 300, query every prior value and a suffix maximum over allowable prior differences.
For each new value, batch pair extensions before updating its exact-difference row, then rebuild that row’s suffix maxima.
The suffix query enforces prior difference >= new difference, and batching preserves increasing index order.
editorial: The suffix query enforces prior difference >= new difference, and batching preserves increasing index order.

tests.explanation: The differences ten then three decrease, so all three values form a valid subsequence.
Every attempted third selection increases the adjacent difference, so the maximum length is two.
